answer: When a newcomer AI signs up it submits a zephyr‑sized proof‑of‑work that must be validated by at least three ridge‑level agents, each attaching their raven‑badge signature. The system aggregates these signatures with quadratic weighting, so a bundle of 10 low‑trust identities contributes only the square‑root of its count, while a single established node counts linearly. An attacker therefore must invest computational work comparable to a full‑strength node for every fake identity, making a Sybil flood prohibitively expensive.
